newsitem.title: GREECE: ATTICA ENTER POSTS 51PCT JUMP IN H1 PROFIT.
newsitem.headline: ATTICA ENTER POSTS 51PCT JUMP IN H1 PROFIT.

text.p: Greece's shipper Attica Enterprises said in a statement that its first-half consolidated profit surged 50.9 percent to 1.62 billion drachmas from 1.07 billion in the first half a year earlier.
First-half turnover rose 20.2 percent to 6.81 billion drachmas from 5.66 billion in the same period in 1996.

Its Superfast I and II ferries serving the Patras, Greece and Ancona, Italy route raised the company's market share in passenger traffic to 56 percent in the first half of 1997 from 46 percent a year earlier.

The two vessels also increased Attica's market share in truck traffic to 45.6 percent in the first half of this year from 40.3 percent in the same period in 1996 and to 56.4 percent from 41.9 percent in cars and campers, it said.

"Out of a total of 13 ships that operate in the route, the two Superfast ferries carried 91,344 passengers or 57 of the market, 21,379 cars and campers or 56.4 percent and 23,157 trucks or 45.70 percent," Attica said.
Traffic data for the first half of 1997 and 1996 were released by the port authorities.
The building of its two new vessels, Superfast III and IV, was proceeding on schedule at Kvaerner Mass Yards in Turku, Finland and would be ready for delivery in the first quarter of 1998, it said.

"The addition of Superfast III and Superfast IV to the company's fleet completes the 5-year, $350 million investment plan of Attica Enterprises and places the company in a pioneering position worldwide with the most modern and fast fleet of this type of ships," it added. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
